Aisha: Heads up — saw a recurrent p95 latency spike on the long-context CI load after last night's runtime deploy. traces point at a KV reclaim scan happening inline during generation which stalls token emission for a few dozen ms. sample log below. anyone else seeing this? :eyes:

Aisha: ```
[2026-03-15T14:21:03Z] kv_reclaim: scanned=1024 reclaimed=12 duration_ms=72
[2026-03-15T14:21:03Z] kv_page_swap: swapped_pages=8 delay_ms=58
hot_entries_scan_ms=48 freelist_lock_wait_ms=12
```

Connor: I'm on it. We did flip the eviction behavior in the pager branch — hybrid LRU/FIFO heuristics went live with the kernel-selection tweak (kernel v3 fast-path enabled). Might have changed pager_window default from 8 -> 32. That would increase scan sizes.

Devon: Repro steps that hit the spike for me: run long-context sustained QPS with bursty prefixes. Quick repro command I used: 
```
./run_perf --model redwood-7b --context 65536 --qps 50 --concurrency 20 --duration 10m
```
When concurrency > 12 the inline reclaim shows up in the generation critical path.

perf-bot: flamegraph uploaded: /perf/2219/kv_scan.svg (shows a big slice in kv::reclaim and freelist mutex)

Liu: hybrid evict can cause reinsert churn if reuse heuristics are too aggressive — FIFO tailing + LRU head leads to repeated scan-and-reinsert cycles under paging pressure. two quick knobs to try: lower pager_window and raise reuse_threshold. Also `kv.pager_max_scan` to cap per-request scan work.

Aisha: I toggled `kv.reuse_threshold=0.8` -> `0.6` and `kv.pager_max_scan=256` in staging and ran the same perf job. p95 dropped from ~240ms to ~42ms, median unchanged. saw ~3x fewer reclaim ops in the logs.

Connor: nice. That suggests the problem is scan amplification not correctness. still want to be cautious about memory growth/regressions — the reuse change trades a bit of memory for latency. Can you paste the before/after reclaim counts?

Aisha: before: reclaimed_total=1834 scans=412 avg_scan_ms=58
after: reclaimed_total=610 scans=129 avg_scan_ms=18

Devon: seems like the kernel selection path also changed page size hinting which can alter worst-case scan windows. I can instrument the pager to emit `scan_budget_remaining` and add metrics for `reinsert_rate` per-shard. will open a small PR.

Liu: long-term fix ideas: 1) decouple reclaim from request-critical path (background compaction + async eviction tokens), 2) per-shard watermarks so a single hot shard doesn't trigger global scans, 3) soft-fallback to a small FIFO drain when under latency SLO.

Connor: agree. action items: Devon to add more granular metrics and a cap on inline scan (PR by EOD), Aisha to run expanded staging with reuse_threshold matrix, Liu to draft background compaction proposal. I'll also roll back the pager_window change if we see more regressions. Meeting to sync tomorrow 9:30 PT.

Aisha: thanks — staging looks stable with the temporary knobs. will keep monitoring; will post updated flamegraph after next run. :thumbsup:

Devon: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/eng/runtime/+/3456 (adds scan_budget_remaining metric and per-shard reinsert counters)

perf-bot: perf run summary: p95_before=238ms p95_after=42ms peak_swap_delay_before=58ms peak_swap_delay_after=9ms

Connor: tagging this for postmortem / perf-regressions board. good catch Aisha. :shipit:
